meta.purpose: Real dated prices so 'cheapest time to book' is answered with evidence, not a guess.
meta.method: Booking.com searches for whole weeks, 2 adults, 1 room, USD, sorted by price, captured 2026-11-25. Only properties that appeared in a captured result block are listed.
meta.caveat: The user's stated window is 2027-02-15 → 2027-03-23. Everything outside that range is excluded. All five windows below sit inside it.

windows.label: 15–22 Feb 2027
windows.note: Starts on the user's preferred arrival date.

windows.label: 15–22 Mar 2027
windows.note: Ends the day before the user's outer limit.

matrix.room_note: Nobu's cheapest week is February, the opposite of the big resorts
W1 is a 1-bedroom suite; W2 is a Deluxe King

most_expensive_week_overall.label: 15–22 Feb 2027
most_expensive_week_overall.evidence: Every large resort is at its highest captured rate; the week contains US Presidents' Day (15 Feb 2027). The link between the holiday and the price is a reasonable reading of the calendar, but the CAUSE is not verified by any source.

derived.anomaly: Nobu at Caesars Palace is the one property that is CHEAPER in W1 ($1,125) than W3 ($1,750). No explanation verified — flagged F-12.
derived.recommendation: If the couple can move the trip from 15 Feb to the 8–15 Mar window, the same suites at the Venetian/Palazzo/Cosmopolitan cost roughly $1,300–$1,500 less for seven nights. That is the single largest cost lever in this plan.
